column1: Stations within 150 km of a county polygon. Position on the river is approximated by latitude (Nile flows north): south = upstream, north = downstream, within 0.15 deg = local. Check Station_assignment for east-west reaches (Sobat, Pibor).
River predictors: lvl = monthly max level as percentile of the station's own record
column2: lvlz = z-score against the same calendar month in other years (removes the seasonal cycle)
column3: exc = share of passes above the station's own 90th percentile (flood-stage proxy)
column4: rise/rise3 = 1- and 3-month change. Altimetry passes are 10-35 days apart so monthly values are under-sampled.

column1: Lag_AUC and Best_thresholds are IN-SAMPLE screening (lag and cut-off picked on all the data) and are optimistic. Use Nested_CV and Models for skill.

Nested_CV: for every held-out year (or county) the lag, direction and threshold are chosen on the other folds only. AUC_lo95/hi95 = bootstrap over whole counties. If the interval includes 0.5 there is no demonstrated skill.

Models: ridge logistic on the best lag of each predictor (lag chosen inside each training fold). "+ county effects" adds a dummy per county; it can only be validated by leaving out years. The BENCHMARK row (a county's own event rate) is the bar to beat: predictors only add value if they beat it.

Risk_ranking: each flood-season month the counties are ranked by out-of-fold model score; recall = share of events falling in the top k, compared with chance (k / counties). lift = precision / base rate.

column2: rain is GSMaP v8 gauge-corrected. Both are county means at 5 km.
